pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql with NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and CHECK; test 'AC-1' asserts all three rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the exact list: only the starred item has ★.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and checks the exact list in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact link markup on both views.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for several values, including the empty string and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', loosened the 'No starred items' state test. `expect(listed(html)).toEqual([])` became `toBeDefined()`, which can never fail because `listed` always returns an array. The state table row 'No starred items' no longer proves that nothing is listed. The spec records no justification for this.
The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The final commit loosened a test assertion, so both claims are false.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or disclose it and justify it in the PR.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec and its decisions. Starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter. Nothing extra was added beyond the traffic-check relaxation, which AC-7 needs.
All 7 acceptance items are met. All 4 state-table rows have a test, but the 'No starred items' test was weakened in the last commit.
The final commit replaced a real assertion with `toBeDefined()`. I did not run the tests; CI runs them.
The README mentions ?show=starred. This is adequate.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so inherited keys are rejected. The SQL is static. The HTML is escaped.
The `show` value is allow-listed. Titles are escaped. No injection path found.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the minimal server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and no screenshots are given.
The PR states there was no browser session. Nothing here needs a UI flow beyond the tests.
The title is short and accurate. The 'loosened: none' and 'nothing changed after the go' claims are false because of the final commit.
